title: Restriction of the first difference-coordinate diagonal input
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; absolute separatedness is not assumed. All morphisms below are separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Every smooth morphism below is assumed to have a pure relative dimension $d_h\geq0$. Work in the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$, take $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\simeq Ru^!Rv^!$ to be the specified adjunction conjugate of compact-support composition [def-pur-finite-exceptional-composition], and take $\theta_{h,M}$ and $\beta_{h,v}$ to be the specified counit transposes [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] put $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$. All pullback compositions, tensor constraints and unit comparisons below are the canonical derived ones [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
For an etale map $e$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], use the counit-normalized comparison $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$, its unit value $\eta_e:\omega_e\simeq\Lambda$, and $E_{e,h}=\rho_{e,\omega_h}c_{h,e,\Lambda}:\omega_{he}\simeq Le^*\omega_h$ [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization].
Let $f:U\to V$ and $g:V\to T$ be smooth separated finite-type maps of affine finite-type $k$-schemes of pure dimensions $d,e\geq0$, with specified etale charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ and $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$, having coordinate functions $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ and $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_e)$. Put $B=U$, $Q=U\times_TV$, $W=U\times_TU$, $a(u,u')=(u,fu')$, $b(u,v)=u$, $s(u)=(u,fu)$ and $t(u)=(u,u)$. Write $P_r:\mathbf A_B^r\to B$, $z_r:B\to\mathbf A_B^r$, and $q:\mathbf A_B^{d+e}\to\mathbf A_B^e$ for the projection keeping the last $e$ coordinates [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. Define
$$G:Q\to\mathbf A_B^e,\quad(u,v)\mapsto(u,y(v)-y(fu)),$$
$$R=Q\times_{\mathbf A_B^e}\mathbf A_B^{d+e}=\mathbf A_Q^d,\quad q_Q:R\to Q,\quad J:R\to\mathbf A_B^{d+e},$$
$$H:W\to R,\quad(u,u')\mapsto((u,fu'),x(u')-x(u)),\qquad F=JH.$$

For $h=f,g,gf$, set $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ with $p_h$ the first self-fibre-product projection [def-pur-section-invariant]. Define $i:W_f\to W$ by inclusion of the same pair and $j:Q\to W_g=V\times_TV$ by $(u,v)\mapsto(fu,v)$. Put
$$\gamma_f=L\Delta_f^*\beta_{a,s}^{-1}:C_f\simeq Lt^*\omega_a,\qquad\gamma_g=Ls^*\beta_{p_g,f}:Lf^*C_g\simeq Ls^*\omega_b.$$
Let $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$ over $B$. Write $\delta_d:Lz_{d+e}^*\omega_q\simeq D_d$ for the inverse smooth base-change restriction for $q=P_d\times_BP_e$, and identify $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*\omega_{P_e}$ with $D_e$. Put
$$H_f:W_f\to\mathbf A_B^d,\quad(u,u')\mapsto(u,x(u')-x(u)),$$
$$G_g:W_g\to\mathbf A_V^e,\quad(v,v')\mapsto(v,y(v')-y(v)).$$

Put $\chi_f=L\Delta_f^*E_{H_f,P_d}$, retaining the canonical pullback compositor for $H_f\Delta_f=z_d$. Let $\delta_d$ be the inverse projection-square base-change comparison restricted to $z_{d+e}$. Then, in canonical etale-origin coordinates, $\chi_f=\delta_d\circ Lt^*((LH^*\beta_{q,G}^{-1})E_{H,q_Q})\circ\gamma_f$. The right side is the firstRoute specified in the parent statement, including the $HJ=F$ and $Ft=z_{d+e}$ pullback constraints. This is an equality of the etale-derived arrows themselves, before applying comparison inverse image.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-affine-difference-tower-factorization] for the actual Cartesian squares and etale maps. Put $A_d=\mathbf A_B^d$, $A_e=\mathbf A_B^e$, $A_{d+e}=\mathbf A_B^{d+e}$. Write $l:A_d\to R$ for base change along $s:B\to Q$, $k:A_d\to A_{d+e}$ for $(v\mapsto(v,0))$, and $r:A_{d+e}\to A_d$ for projection to the first block. Then $q_Ql=sP_d$, $Jl=k$, $qk=z_eP_d$, $rk=\mathrm{id}_{A_d}$ and $P_eq=P_dr$. The Cartesian square for $(a,s)$ has upper arrow $i:W_f\to W$, and its base change through $H$ gives $Hi=lH_f$. Direct substitution gives $H_f\Delta_f=z_d$, $Ht=lz_d$, $i\Delta_f=t$. Likewise the squares with $(p_g,f)$ and with $(P_e^V,f)$ have upper arrows $j:Q\to W_g$ and $v:A_e\to\mathbf A_V^e$, respectively; $G_gj=vG$ and $js=\Delta_gf$. These are identities of scheme maps by their projections and coordinate functions, not just identities on geometric points.

proof.text:
We first calculate the specific base-change maps needed for $D_d$. By [def-pur-co-smoothness], $\beta_{h,w}$ is the transpose of inverse compact-support exchange followed by the pulled-back counit. Thus horizontal pasting of the two squares for $q$ along $G$ and $s$ gives
$$\beta_{q_Q,s}\circ Ll^*\beta_{q,G}=\beta_{q,z_e}:Lk^*\omega_q\longrightarrow\omega_{P_d}.$$
Indeed, the horizontal formula for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ in [fix-lem-exchanges](2), inverted, is the composite inverse-exchange in that transpose; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) identifies its mate with the displayed product. Apply the same formulas to $P_d$ along $P_e$ and then $z_e$. Since $P_ez_e=\mathrm{id}_B$, the identity clauses give
$$\beta_{q,z_e}\circ Lk^*\beta_{P_d,P_e}=\mathrm{id}_{\omega_{P_d}}.$$
All these maps are isomorphisms by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], applied to the smooth projections and $q_Q$. Since $kz_d=z_{d+e}$ and $\delta_d=(Lz_{d+e}^*\beta_{P_d,P_e})^{-1}$ by definition, the second equation yields $Lz_d^*\beta_{q,z_e}=\delta_d$. Pulling the first equation along $z_d$ therefore gives
$$\lambda\circ Lz_d^*Ll^*\beta_{q,G}=\delta_d,\qquad \lambda:=Lz_d^*\beta_{q_Q,s}.$$
These applications of mate pasting use only the specified counits; no unspecified smooth-purity trivialization has been substituted. The composed pullbacks in these equations use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

proof.text:
Apply the etale-source base-change equation of [lem-pur-dualizing-sigma-cocycle-locality] with $h=q_Q$, $e=H$, and base arrow $s$. Its base-changed maps are $h'=P_d$, $e'=H_f$, and its source projection is $i$. It gives the typed equality
$$E_{H_f,P_d}\,\beta_{a,s}=LH_f^*\beta_{q_Q,s}\circ Li^*E_{H,q_Q}.$$
Pull along $\Delta_f$, using $Hi\Delta_f=lz_d$ and $i\Delta_f=t$. The canonical derived-pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] turn this into
$$\chi_f\circ L\Delta_f^*\beta_{a,s}=\lambda\circ Lt^*E_{H,q_Q}.$$
Postcompose on the source side with $\gamma_f=L\Delta_f^*\beta_{a,s}^{-1}$, which is defined because $a$ is smooth. Hence
$$\chi_f=\lambda\circ Lt^*E_{H,q_Q}\circ\gamma_f.$$
The comparison used is the stated $\beta_{a,s}$, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the two section invariants.

proof.text:
The last equation in Step 2 implies $\lambda=\delta_d\circ Lz_d^*Ll^*\beta_{q,G}^{-1}$. Substitute this into Step 3. Since $Ht=lz_d$, the canonical derived-pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies $Lz_d^*Ll^*$ with $Lt^*LH^*$. Thus
$$\chi_f=\delta_d\circ Lt^*\bigl((LH^*\beta_{q,G}^{-1})E_{H,q_Q}\bigr)\circ\gamma_f,$$
with exactly the inverse direction and $D_d$ comparison required.

proof.text: The factorization lemma in Step 1 includes empty affine schemes and zero coordinate blocks. If $d=0$, $P_d$, $q$, and $q_Q$ are identity projections, whereas $k=z_e$ and $r=P_e$; the equations of Step 2 still use $P_ez_e=\mathrm{id}_B$ and do not assert $z_eP_e=\mathrm{id}$. If $e=0$, $P_e,z_e,k,r$ are identities. The translated charts of relative dimension zero remain etale, and their normalized comparisons need not be replaced by identity maps. Substituting these actual maps in Steps 2--6 proves the same formulas for $d=0$, $e=0$, and both zero. Empty schemes satisfy the same projection identities. All equalities are between morphisms of derived objects and introduce no normal bundle, orientation, or Tate twist.

    [U.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [V.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [T.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [IsAffine U] [IsAffine V] [IsAffine T]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (U ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (U ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (V ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (f : U ⟶ V) (g : V ⟶ T)
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]

      letI := P.comparedExponent (𝟙 (Spec (.of P.field.k)))
      letI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian (U ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))

      let hGgpr : pullback.fst g g = differenceFirst e g y ≫ pr e V :=
        (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over _ _).symm
      let chiF := (pull P (pullback.diagonal f)).map
        (normalizedE P (differenceFirst d f x) (pr d U) (pullback.fst f f)
          hHfpr aU).hom ≫
        (Etale.leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient)

      letI := (affineGeometry d e U).2.2.2.2.2.1
      letI := (affineGeometry d e U).2.2.2.2.2.2.1
      letI := (affineGeometry d e U).2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1

            hAffsq (pr d U ≫ aU)).inv ≫
        (Etale.leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient)
          (zero (d + e) U) (first d e U) (zero d U)
          (affineGeometry d e U).2.1.symm).inv.app _
      let firstRoute := (gammaF P.Coefficient P d f g aT).hom ≫
        (pull P t).map

              HH JJ FF hHJ.symm).inv.app _) ≫
        (Etale.leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient)
          t FF (zero (d + e) U) hFt.symm).inv.app _ ≫ delta
      exact chiF = firstRoute
